Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: Employees hid question papers in shoes, paid Rs 8,000 each
Article Text:

How the papers allegedly got out

Leak exposed a day before exam

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles, with two employees paid Rs 8,000 each to smuggle out the confidential examination material, according to a chargesheet filed by Thane City police.The chargesheet, filed before a Bhiwandi court on Friday, names 18 accused, including alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta, and lays out how investigators traced the leak from the printing press to those allegedly trying to sell the papers in Maharashtra. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while two others, Ashok Sav and Prakash Misal, remain absconding, police said.According to the chargesheet, the leak was traced to Mahim Patran Pvt Ltd, an Agra-based printing press tasked with producing the confidential TET examination material.Between June 15 and 17, two employees and a former staffer allegedly concealed folded question papers inside their shoe insoles while leaving the premises. Security guards frisked their clothes but allegedly did not check their footwear, allowing the papers to be taken outside, the chargesheet said.The state had prepared four separate sets of question papers for the two TET papers to maintain confidentiality and allow one set to be selected on examination day.Investigators allege that all four sets were nevertheless taken out of the press.The employees were allegedly paid Rs 8,000 each and promised land plots in Agra in return for stealing the papers, according to the chargesheet.The racket came to light on June 27, a day before the TET was scheduled to be held. Deputy commissioner of Police Pavan Bansod received information that three men were allegedly trying to sell question papers to a Bhiwandi resident.Police then laid a trap using decoy personnel in Kongaon and detained the suspects, recovering four sets of question papers. Officials of the Maharashtra state council of examination later verified that the seized material matched the actual TET paper.The examination, scheduled for June 28, was subsequently postponed.Police have booked the accused under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy, along with Maharashtra laws dealing with examination malpractice. A special investigation team is probing the case.Investigators have identified Gupta, a former coaching-class teacher, as the alleged mastermind. Police said he had previously been implicated in another examination paper leak in Odisha.The chargesheet cites money trails, technical evidence and the recovery of an original question paper from the Bihar residence of a relative of Gupta as evidence in the alleged supply chain. Police said a supplementary chargesheet would be filed as the investigation continues.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles. Two employees were allegedly paid Rs 8,000 each and promised land plots in Agra in return for stealing the papers. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while two others, Ashok Sav and Prakash Misal, remain absconding.

Article Title: Over 37 lakh appeals pending after Bengal SIR: EC tells Supreme Court
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision remain pending.The poll panel told the apex court in its response affidavit that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.This comes after a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana sought the poll panel's response to a plea seeking disclosure of assembly constituency-wise data on claims and objections filed by voters whose names were deleted during the SIR exercise.A total of 38,20,683 appeals had been filed against orders relating to the SIR of electoral rolls. Of these, 1,02,231 appeals had been disposed of, leaving 37,18,452 pending, the poll panel said.The affidavit, however, did not provide a break-up of the appeals filed by electors whose names were deleted and those filed against the inclusion of names in the electoral rolls.Prasenjit Bose, who filed the affidavit, claimed that more than 58 lakh electors were excluded during the enumeration phase of the SIR exercise in West Bengal.He added that while 9.64 lakh applications for inclusion (Forms 6 and 6A) and over 99,000 applications for deletion (Form 7) were received during the claims and objections phase, only around 1.82 lakh additions were reflected in the final electoral roll published on February 28.On August 25, the top court directed the Election Commission to submit data on the pendency and disposal of appeals before tribunals challenging exclusion or inclusion in electoral rolls.Observing that these appeals needed to be adjudicated in a time-bound manner, the bench had asked the poll panel to explain what steps were being taken to streamline the mechanism for disposing of pending appeals and how many additional tribunals were required.The EC data submitted to the court showed that 34.13 lakh Form 6 applications had been filed between December 17, 2025, when the draft electoral roll was published, and August 7, 2026.Form 6 is the statutory application for inclusion of a name in the electoral roll.On April 24, the apex court asked the appellate tribunals to give out-of-turn hearings to those who made a case for urgent hearing against deletion from electoral rolls after the SIR.Approximately 700 judicial officers from West Bengal and neighbouring Odisha and Jharkhand were deployed to deal with around 60 lakh claims and objections.Later, the chief justice of the Calcutta high court, on the direction of the top court, set up 19 tribunals headed by former high court chief justices and judges to decide the appeals.
Article Summary: The Election Commission told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls remain pending. The poll panel told the apex court that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.

Article Title: 'I knew this was the end of my career': Ajit Doval recalls when his agents were captured by China
Article Text:
Ajit Doval recalls China custody episode: ‘I knew this was the end of my career’

NEW DELHI: National security advisor Ajit Doval on Saturday recalled one of the most difficult moments of his early career, when a group of operatives sent across the border went missing and were later found to be in Chinese custody.Speaking as the chief guest at the two-day convocation ceremony of IIT Roorkee, NSA Doval said he was deeply worried after receiving no information about the group's whereabouts.He said: “We got no reports of any avalanche or anything. It was a matter of deep worry and concern. But I got a telephone call from the headquarters, and my boss told me, "Have you sent some people across?" I said, "I do not know. They must be coming. They should have come in five or six days, but now it is about ten or eleven days." He said, "They are in Chinese custody now." They were caught by the Chinese and interrogated. Anyway, the Chinese returned them, probably after some talks or negotiations, or a deal must have been struck. So, they returned totally shattered, in shambles. And an inquiry was started. I knew that this was the end of my career. I was still in my twenties, and I had to start a new career.I saw the incident as something very unprofessional.”Doval said an inquiry was later conducted and he was not held responsible for the incident.“Anyway, the inquiry was over. I wasn't found at fault. Probably, I had done everything right. The sketches and the maps that were given to us by the headquarters had some defects and mistakes in them. That is how it happened," the NSA added.He also spoke about the opportunities available to today's younger generation, particularly with rapid advances in technology."You may not be conscious of the fact that in the last 1000 years, you are the luckiest generation, which is going to have so many opportunities. Generations before you were struggling under slavery. They did not have those opportunities which opened up for you. And not only that, things have changed here, but globally things have changed for the better for you... You are coming at an age when technology will be the most important driving factor in any country's or society's growth and progress," Ajit Doval said.The two-day convocation began at IIT Roorkee on Saturday, with degrees set to be awarded to 2,701 students. NSA Doval attended the event as the chief guest.
Article Summary: National security advisor Ajit Doval recalls one of the most difficult moments of his early career. Group of operatives sent across the border went missing and were later found to be in Chinese custody. NSA Doval said he was deeply worried after receiving no information about the group's whereabouts.

NEW DELHI: A fire broke out at a helipad terminal in Katra, the base camp for pilgrims visiting the Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine in Jammu and Kashmir 's Reasi district, early Sunday, officials said.The fire started around 3:15 am, apparently due to a short circuit, and was brought under control within 30 minutes through the joint efforts of terminal staff, security personnel and fire and emergency services, officials said, according to news agency PTI.The helipad terminal, an important transit point for pilgrims travelling to the shrine atop the Trikuta hills, was closed at the time of the incident.Some computers at the ticket counter and a coffee shop were destroyed in the fire, officials added.The extent of the damage is being assessed. Article Title: SC 'banyan tree' of environmental justice: CJI Surya Kant
Article Text:
Environmental issues have no geographical limitations, said CJI Surya Kant

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the right to a pollution-free environment be considered a fundamental right? Yes, absolutely No, not necessary 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Terming Supreme Court the "banyan tree" of environmental justice for its role in protecting the environment and ecology, CJI Surya Kant Saturday said conservation and development are not in conflict with each other and there is need to maintain balance between them.Addressing the inaugural session of 'The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics' organised by NGT, he said there are constitutional provisions for protection of environment, but words in a constitution are only seeds which need the nurturing waters of judicial wisdom to sprout into life and SC has played that role."And it is here that SC has stood tall as the banyan tree of environmental justice, with roots deep in our civilisational ethos and branches sheltering the rights of unseen generations. It has over the decades championed the idea that progress without preservation is but a mirage that vanishes in the desert of ecological ruin. Its rulings underscore how safeguarding nature is not an act of altruism but of self-preservation, an investment in the very continuity of life. "Highlighting its proactive approach, he said SC has made the right to a pollution-free environment a fundamental right by reading it directly into Article 21 ."That same pattern has carried us to the present day, where SC recently articulated the idea of 'eco-centric proportionality', postulating that environmental protection must be rigorous yet intelligent enough to engage with the world as it exists. This notion has advanced the most pragmatic approach of permitting development solely in conjunction with enforceable conditions, expert oversight, restoration, compensatory afforestation and accountability."Recent Indian jurisprudence on climate has brought this question into sharper constitutional focus by recognising the adverse effects of climate change can impact fundamental rights of equality, livelihood, health and conditions necessary for meaningful enjoyment of these rights," he added.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant said conservation and development are not in conflict with each other and there is need to maintain balance between them. He said there are constitutional provisions for protection of environment, but words in a constitution are only seeds which need the nurturing waters of judicial wisdom.

NEW DELHI: Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General NS Raja Subramani on Saturday said “as technology is changing, it is not the most brilliant person but the person who has the ability to adapt to changing circumstances, ability to learn, and ability to change with the times will succeed”. Addressing graduates at the IIT Roorkee convocation, the CDS said “Bharat is not a geography. It is a responsibility which generations before you have carried, and you will carry as you navigate this world.”Explaining the meaning of ‘BHARAT’, Gen Subramani said, 'B' stands for build. Be a builder, don't just be a technology consumer; be a technology creator; 'H' stands for harness, harness the power of technology, the power of AI, the power of space, the power of your intelligence, and harness the power of your teams; 'A' stands for adaptability, which I have already spoken about, adapt to the world, adapt to changing circumstances; 'R' stands for research, research must have outcomes. It has to be related to what the country requires; and 'A stands for Atmanirbharta (self-reliance).”Explaining the last alphabet in BHARAT, Gen Subramani said, “'T' stands for taking responsibility. Take responsibility for yourself, take responsibility for your actions, and take responsibility to contribute, even in a small measure, to take our nation forward.”“If each one of us contributes like the droplets of a river, the nation will continue to move forward, grow, and achieve the dream of Viksit Bharat 2047," he told students.He urged future engineers and technologists to focus on developing resilient systems.The CDS also introduced the acronym “DHARA” to describe the transformations shaping the world. “I want to speak about the changing world, and I'll give you an acronym for that. That is Dhara. What I mean by Dhara is D - disruptive; H - hyper-connectedness; A - asymmetry; R - realignment; and A - autonomy.”“The world is undergoing enormous disruption. Technology is changing faster than we can catch up. You, as graduates, will have to learn, unlearn, relearn, adapt, and remain curious throughout if you want to keep up with the changing world,” Gen Subramani said.
Article Summary: Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General NS Raja Subramani on Saturday said ‘as technology is changing, it is not the most brilliant person but the person who has the ability to adapt to changing circumstances’ ‘Bharat is not a geography. It is a responsibility which generations before you have carried, and you will carry as you navigate this world’

Article Title: ‘System’ does not want students to ask questions: Rahul Gandhi offers to join MP teacher aspirants’ protest in Indore
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi at his Indore session of 'Chhatron Ki Goonj'event

Rahul alleges ‘system’ controls institutions

NEW DELHI: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday offered to participate in the ongoing protest by teacher job aspirants in Madhya Pradesh, while alleging that the "system" was preventing students from raising questions.Speaking at the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme in Indore, Rahul Gandhi said students were being targeted because they questioned the functioning of institutions and the opportunities available to them. His remarks came amid continuing concerns among students and job aspirants over recruitment and education-related issues in Madhya Pradesh.Gandhi said, "The system feels threatened by students. Why? Because students ask questions. A student asks how Amit Shah’s son became the Chairman of the Cricket Association. A student asks how two individuals managed to capture the entire business landscape of India. A student asks why the judiciary and other institutions fail to do their jobs, or why the Election Commission isn't performing its duties. That is why the system does not want students; it wants 'Andhbhakts'. An andhbhakt is the antithesis of a student. While a student asks questions and remains curious, an andhbhakt lives in a delusional world of their own.While a student is fearless, an andhbhakt is a coward."Rahul Gandhi also alleged that a network of political, bureaucratic and business interests controls institutions across the country. He said the struggle by students was against what he described as the "system"."The struggle is against the system. What is this system? The system has various layers. At the top level sit six individuals who run it. Narendra Modi ji—he handles the intimidation, the acts of beating students, the use of nail-studded batons, and the firing of pellet guns; Amit Shah ji runs it; he is the enforcer. This is Ajit Doval ji, the National Security Advisor. In informal conversations, he says that to control India, one only needs to control 500 people. He has taken control of India's telephones, WhatsApp, and Facebook communications; he orchestrates phone tapping and passes the information to Amit Shah ji and Narendra Modi ji. In the middle is Mohan Bhagwat ji, who deals with ideology; his organization receives thousands of crores of rupees to run schools, colleges, and institutions. Then, on one side, there is Adani ji, and on the other, Ambani ji...The system has placed its own people in every single institution..."Rahul Gandhi's remarks were made during his interaction with students at the fifth edition of his ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ initiative in Indore. The initiative has focused on issues concerning education, examinations, recruitment and employment. Gandhi had earlier invited students, parents and teachers to share their experiences and concerns about the education system ahead of the Indore event.‘System designed to protect students is attacking them’Rahul Gandhi also responded to a student who raised concerns over the functioning of universities and alleged lack of transparency."As I just mentioned, students feel that the very system designed to help and protect them, and to safeguard universities and colleges, is the one attacking them," Rahul Gandhi said.Interacting with him, a student said, "Absolutely. The universities are simply unable to cooperate; there is fraud going on everywhere. There is a complete lack of transparency. All we want is a proper solution to the issues we have brought to you so that all our problems can be resolved..."The Indore programme is part of Gandhi's ongoing ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ outreach, which has previously been held in Kota, Dehradun, Prayagraj and Pune. The initiative has focused on student concerns including examination irregularities, recruitment delays and employment.Gandhi's Indore event was shifted to September 19 after the Congress said permission to use Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium had been denied. The party subsequently arranged an alternative venue for the programme.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi offered to participate in teacher job aspirants' protest in Madhya Pradesh. He said students were being targeted because they questioned the functioning of institutions and the opportunities available to them. Gandhi also alleged that a network of political, bureaucratic and business interests controls institutions across the country.

Article Title: DUSU election results: BJP hails ABVP's 'splendid victory'; Congress claims vote tampering

NEW DELHI: Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) on Saturday won three of the four central panel posts in the Delhi University Students' Union election, with its candidate Yash Dabas elected president.Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen, who was denied a ticket by the Congress-affiliated NSUI, won the vice-president's post.Union home minister Amit Shah hailed the victory saying "Heartfelt congratulations to all the dedicated workers of the council on the splendid victory of in the Delhi University Students' Union elections.This victory reflects the unwavering trust of the youth in the council's ideology of "Nation First" and its commitment to student welfare. I am fully confident that the council's workers, drawing new energy from this victory and following the ideals of Swami Vivekananda Ji, will continue to relentlessly advance the cause of student interests and nation-building."BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday congratulated the ABVP for its victory."Congratulations to all my young friends at Delhi University on ABVP’s historic victory in the DUSU elections! This victory reflects the youth’s continued faith in positive and constructive student politics, rooted in the spirit of Nation First, and their strong resolve to contribute to the vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat’.My best wishes to the victorious candidates and everyone who worked tirelessly to make this victory possible," Nabin said in a post on X.Defence minister Rajnath Singh also congratulated the ABVP on its victory in the Delhi University Students' Union elections."Heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all workers on the splendid success of @ABVPVoice in the Delhi University Students' Union elections. This victory is a symbol of the unwavering faith of the youth in the Nation First policy. I am confident that ABVP will continue to work with the same dedication in commitment to student interests, national service, and nation-building. Heartfelt congratulations to the entire ABVP team and best wishes for a bright future!" the defence minister said in a post on X.NSUI president Vinod Jakhar alleged that the Delhi University administration was supporting the ABVP and accused officials of attempting to influence the counting process in the Delhi University Students' Union elections.Jakhar claimed that the lead held by NSUI's presidential candidate Vijay Shankar Meena was being gradually reduced and that the pace of counting was being deliberately slowed.He said, “The Delhi University administration has come out in support of ABVP! There have been continuous attempts at rigging and influencing the counting process. The lead that NSUI's candidate for the president's post, Vijay Shankar Meena, has held for a long time is being gradually whittled down, and the pace of counting is also being slowed. This tampering with the students' mandate will not be tolerated.”
Article Summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) on Saturday won three of the four central panel posts in the Delhi University Students' Union election. Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen, who was denied a ticket by the Congress-affiliated NSUI, won the vice-president's post.

BENGALURU: Hundreds of school-children commuting along the Varthur-Gunjur stretch of SH-35 endured a harrowing Thursday as severe traffic congestion delayed school buses by up to 40 minutes in the morning and left students stranded on roads for hours while returning home. A 4km drive took 2.5 hours, stuck mostly in traffic.The stretch hosts 18-20 big schools, with many conducting mid-term examinations. Several students took up to 1.5 hours more to return home. Some schools accommodated affected students by providing extra time to complete exams.The Varthur-Gunjur stretch, part of SH-35, is undergoing infrastructure works being executed by Karnataka Road Development Corporation. However, residents say the corridor continues to be plagued by bottlenecks, damaged road surfaces, large craters and unmanaged traffic, making the daily commute unpredictable. Parents said Thursday’s situation highlighted how ongoing infrastructure issues were directly affecting schoolchildren.Priti Singh, a resident of Candor Landmark Apartments, said the biggest concern was that schools had exams. “It is unbelievable an area contributing significantly to the city’s economy continues to suffer from such poor infrastructure,” she added.Another resident, Pavitra Holla, said children were spending more time in traffic than in classrooms. “Today, some children took nearly 2.5 hours to cover just 4km from school. They are exhausted, parents are worried and there is no end in sight. There are no proper roads, heavy vehicles move during school hours, traffic management is absent and basic infrastructure is missing. Children are forced to sit in dust and traffic for hours,” she said. Holla added that while congestion has been a long-standing issue in the area, conditions have deteriorated in the past two weeks.For some parents, the situation left them with little choice but to abandon school buses and attempt the journey themselves.Swati Kumari, another resident of Candor Landmark, said she waited nearly 45 minutes for her son’s school bus before deciding to take him on a two-wheeler. “My son studies in a school less than 2km away from home. Though his school ends by 2.45pm, he’s been reaching home around 4.30pm in the past month. The scooter ride took me more than an hour to travel barely 1km,” she said.Calling the commute unsafe, Kumari said parents are increasingly worried about putting young children on two-wheelers given recent accidents and the condition of the road.
Article Summary: Severe traffic congestion delayed school buses by up to 40 minutes in the morning. A 4km drive took 2.5 hours, stuck mostly in traffic. The stretch hosts 18-20 big schools, with many conducting mid-term examinations. Parents said Thursday’s situation highlighted how ongoing infrastructure issues were directly affecting schoolchildren.

Article Title: "Take that cross off your neck": Fans trash Sophie Cunningham over Sydney Sweeney comments as WNBA debate intensifies

Sophie Cunningham’s comments spark divided fan reactions

Sophie Cunningham has weighed in on Sydney Sweeney ’s controversial sports betting ad, but the reaction online has become a story of its own. While the Indiana Fever guard questioned the campaign’s authenticity and raised concerns about its message, some fans rushed to defend Sweeney. Others turned the discussion into a debate about women in sports, beauty standards and why the ad drew so much attention.Cunningham shared her thoughts on Sweeney’s Novig campaign during the premiere of her revamped podcast, No Hesitation, which she co-hosts with Drew Hanlen. The ad features Sweeney appearing nude while trying different sports and repeating the phrase, “Just sports.”Cunningham questioned whether Sweeney genuinely follows sports betting and described the campaign as inauthentic. Still, she made it clear that her criticism of the ad did not mean she disliked the actress.“I have so many takes,” Cunningham said. “First of all, like, does she even gamble on sports? Like, it’s just so inauthentic. You know what I mean? Am I surprised of how she represented the brand? No. That’s what she’s made her whole career off — and, hey, don’t get me wrong. I like her. Everyone knows she is beautiful; she is hot. She clearly has my chest.”Cunningham also acknowledged Sweeney’s right to make her own choices, adding, “I really like her,” before explaining that the campaign was not to her taste.Hanlen suggested Sweeney was following a familiar marketing approach, pointing to her previous American Eagle campaign. Cunningham then questioned why women were particularly upset, given that the ad appeared to target men.“But why are girls mad?” Cunningham said. “That is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad? It is a gambling ad. Men, sports, pretty much naked women. Like, of course, that’s gonna draw attention. Again, do I agree with it? Morally, I think it’s kind of weird, but to each their own. Go do your thing, sis.”She later stressed that she did not believe the campaign was intended to undermine women in sports. Cunningham also praised athletes who challenge traditional beauty standards and encourage young girls to embrace their bodies.Cunningham’s take quickly became a talking point online, with fans split over whether Sweeney’s ad deserved criticism or was simply another marketing campaign.One commenter argued that the ad was simply doing what sports betting promotions are designed to do, writing, “It’s a sports betting ad look at it for what it is. No different that beer ads or hooters girls and chicken. Its has nothing to do with Women sports”Another added, "Sophie, please take that cross off your neck. I know exactly what you’re, nothing but a puppet for the elite. You stand for absolutely nothing and believe that God made you tall so you could play basketball. Full blown hypocrite."Another fan suggested jealousy was driving the backlash, claiming, “The ones that are mad are just jealous. That's all. It is just like all the women in the WNBA. It's pure jealousy. They don't know how to handle it and so they act like children”Others took a more provocative approach. One user wrote, “Threesome with Cunningham and Sweeney would be the ultimate dream,” while another commented, “Sidney is hotter than fish grease. She can’t help herself.”Some reactions focused on the campaign’s political and cultural implications. One commenter wrote, “Because she’s white. If she was black nobody would complain. Weird agenda type shit”Another fan suggested a joint campaign featuring both women, posting, “Now do an ad with Sophie AND Sydney in it together! The libal lefts heads will explode like in that movie Scanners 🤣🤣🤣🤣”Not every response focused on the controversy. One user questioned the promotion itself, writing, “Why is nobody talking about the $25 credit? It's sad. $200 in the average.”The comments show how Cunningham’s remarks have sparked a broader online argument about advertising, women in sports and public reactions to Sweeney’s campaign. While fans remain divided, the debate has pushed the Novig ad far beyond its original sports betting pitch.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham questioned the authenticity of Sydney Sweeney’s Novig sports betting ad. The Indiana Fever guard questioned whether Sweeney genuinely follows sports betting. Some fans rushed to defend Sweeney, while others turned the discussion into a debate about women in sports and beauty standards.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “My family kept me grounded when the whole world was screaming my name.” - How Ryan Coleman-Williams turned unconditional family backing into college football superstardom
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “My family kept me grounded when the whole world was screaming my name.” - How Ryan Coleman-Williams turned unconditional family backing into college football superstardom

How Ryan Coleman-Williams and Ryan Williams Sr. built their football connection

Why Ryan Williams reclassified from 2025 to 2024

What Ryan Williams did at Alabama at only 17

How Ryan Williams’ family stayed part of his rise

Ryan Coleman-Williams was already one of the biggest names in Alabama high school football when he made a decision that changed his path. The Saraland star left high school a year early, moved from the 2025 recruiting class to 2024 and joined Alabama at just 17. The move came with plenty of attention, but his family had been part of his football journey long before he reached Tuscaloosa. His father, Ryan Williams Sr., had played college football, while his mother, Tiffany Coleman, and his grandparents helped give him the support and structure he needed from a young age.Football was familiar territory in the Williams family. Ryan Williams Sr. played at Auburn after a standout high school career at B.C. Rain in Mobile. He later transferred to Copiah-Lincoln Community College and finished his college career at Louisiana Tech. His playing career gave him a clear understanding of the demands that came with trying to reach the next level.But Ryan Coleman-Williams’ development was not only about his father’s football background. ESPN reported that Williams lived with his paternal grandparents, Robert and Catherine Williams, while his father was away at college.His mother, Tiffany Coleman, also spoke about the role the family played in shaping his personality.“He’s an old soul,” Coleman told ESPN. “People are like, ‘He’s so mature to be 17.’ His grandparents had a lot to do with that. His maturity and foundation came from them.”That family support became especially important as Williams’ football career began moving faster than most teenagers could imagine.At Saraland High School, he became one of the most productive players in the state. Alabama’s official profile says he had 198 receptions for 3,486 yards and 49 receiving touchdowns during his high school career. He also rushed for 1,082 yards and 25 touchdowns.Williams originally belonged to the 2025 recruiting class. He had already committed to Alabama, but in 2023 he and his family decided that he would finish high school early and join the Crimson Tide sooner than planned.The decision was not made suddenly. ESPN reported that Williams told Saraland coach Jeff Kelly about the move in July 2023, although the decision was kept private while the team continued its season. Williams officially announced the reclassification in December.Kelly said the family handled the decision carefully because Williams did not want it to become a distraction for his teammates.“I think it speaks volumes about who he is,” Kelly told ESPN. “He didn’t want it to be out there because he didn’t want it to be a distraction for his teammates. We had a team that had a chance to win another state title. He and his family did a tremendous job keeping that decision private.”The timing also made sense from a football point of view. Williams had already achieved almost everything possible at the high school level. In 2023, he helped Saraland win another Class 6A state title and finished his high school career with huge numbers.The Alabama Sports Writers Association later named him Mr. Football for the second straight year, making him the first two-time winner of the award.Joining Alabama meant stepping into a completely different level of football. Williams was only 17 during his freshman season, while competing against players who were several years older.He showed that the age gap did not stop him.In September 2024, Williams caught a 75-yard touchdown pass from Jalen Milroe against Georgia in front of more than 100,000 fans at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Alabama won 41-34, and the play became one of the defining moments of Williams’ first college season.Alabama’s official records from that season show just how fast he adjusted. He finished his freshman campaign with 48 catches for 865 yards and eight touchdowns, according to the university’s later player profile. He also earned freshman All-America recognition.The early success was not completely unexpected. Before he even played a college game, Alabama had already listed Williams as a five-star recruit and one of the country’s top receiving prospects. The university said he was among the five-star players added to its 2024 recruiting class.The numbers tell only part of Williams’ story. His family had been around him throughout the long process that took him from Saraland to Alabama.That was clear when he officially signed with Alabama in February 2024. Local outlet Call News published a photograph of Williams with his father Ryan Sr., mother Tiffany Coleman, grandmother Catherine Williams and stepmother Cortney Williams at the signing ceremony.His grandmother has also spoken about how unusual his focus was even as a young child. She recalled that when Williams was in kindergarten, he was already eager to help teachers while other children were playing.That same focus later showed up on the football field.Williams did not have to wait until college to become a star. At Saraland, he won Alabama Mr. Football twice and became one of the most closely watched high school players in the state. His family then supported a difficult decision to leave school early and take on college football at an age when most players are still preparing for their final high school season.That is what makes Ryan Williams’ rise from Saraland to Alabama especially striking. His story is not only about spectacular catches or becoming a college football name at 17. It is also about a young player making an unusually early jump while having his parents, grandparents and family around him throughout the process.
Article Summary: Ryan Coleman-Williams was one of the biggest names in Alabama high school football. The Saraland star left high school a year early, moved from the 2025 recruiting class to 2024 and joined Alabama at just 17. His family had been part of his football journey long before he reached Tuscaloosa.

Article Title: Victoria Beckham and David Beckham bought an 11,500-sq-ft Beverly Hills villa for $22 million; after 11 years, it sold for $33 million in an off-market deal
Article Text:
Victoria Beckham and David Beckham bought an 11,500-sq-ft Beverly Hills villa for $22 million; after 11 years, it sold for $33 million in an off-market deal

How much did David Beckham and Victoria Beckham pay for their Beverly Hills home

What did David Beckham and Victoria Beckham’s Beverly Hills villa include

Why did David Beckham and Victoria Beckham sell the Beverly Hills mansion

How much profit did David Beckham and Victoria Beckham make from the Beverly Hills sale

David and Victoria Beckham’s Beverly Hills mansion sold for about $33.1 million in 2018, ending an 11-year run at the California home. The couple had bought the Italian-style villa in 2007, around the time David Beckham moved to the US to play for LA Galaxy. Property records and reports put their purchase price at about $18.2 million, meaning the sale brought them nearly $15 million more before taxes, fees and other costs. The deal was completed off-market, with the buyer listed through a limited liability company, keeping the new owner’s identity private.David Beckham and Victoria Beckham bought the Beverly Hills property in 2007 after David moved to Los Angeles to begin his Major League Soccer career with LA Galaxy. The home was an Italian villa-style property tucked away behind large gates and a private drive.The purchase price is one area where different reports have given different numbers. The Los Angeles Times reported that the Beckhams paid $18.2 million for the house. Other websites have since repeated a $22 million figure, but the $18.2 million figure is the one backed by the 2018 property reporting from the Los Angeles Times.The house gave the family a private base in Los Angeles while David played in the US. Victoria Beckham was also building her career outside football, first through fashion and later through her own clothing label.The property had about 11,500 to more than 13,000 square feet of living space, depending on the source. It had six bedrooms, multiple living areas, a library, an elevator and a media and music room. The house was also surrounded by gates and landscaping that gave the family a high level of privacy.The size of the home was only part of what made it notable. Its layout was designed for a large family and for entertaining, with several rooms spread across the property.The villa had six bedrooms and about nine to 10 bathrooms, with reports differing slightly on the exact bathroom count. There was also a library, a media and music room, formal living and dining spaces and an elevator.Outside, the property had a swimming pool and large private grounds. Its position behind iron gates and at the end of a private drive meant visitors could not simply see the house from the street.The home also became closely linked with the Beckham family’s years in Los Angeles. Their children lived there during the family’s time in the city, while David continued his football career and Victoria worked on her growing fashion business.The house was not simply a short-term stop after David’s move to the US. The couple kept it for more than a decade, even after David’s playing career in Los Angeles had ended.By the time the house was sold, the family’s life had changed considerably. David Beckham retired from professional football in 2013, while Victoria Beckham’s fashion business had become an increasingly important part of her career in London.The family also had a growing connection to the UK, where they had a home in Holland Park and a country property in the Cotswolds. Their children were also spending more of their time in Britain.David’s business interests later brought the family closer to Miami. He became a co-owner of Inter Miami CF, giving him another major reason to spend time in South Florida.That made the Beverly Hills property less central to the family’s life. Instead of putting it through a traditional public listing, the Beckhams sold it privately.The Los Angeles Times reported in October 2018 that the house had been sold off-market for about $33.1 million. The buyer appeared in property records through a limited liability company, so the identity of the person or people behind the purchase was not publicly disclosed.The private sale also meant there was no long public listing process for the house. The deal was completed in September 2018, after the Beckhams had owned the property for about 11 years.Using the reported $18.2 million purchase price and the roughly $33.1 million sale price, the Beckhams made about $14.9 million in gross profit on the property before transaction costs, taxes, renovations and other expenses.The sale therefore represented a rise of roughly 82% in the property’s price over the 11-year holding period, although that does not mean the couple took home the full increase as profit.Mansion Global also reported that the home had been quietly shopped around before the eventual transaction and confirmed that it was sold without being publicly listed. The buyer was recorded as a Delaware limited liability company.The Beverly Hills sale also fits into a wider change in the Beckhams’ US property interests. In 2020, David and Victoria bought a full-floor residence at Miami’s One Thousand Museum for $19.8 million. The Zaha Hadid-designed tower became part of their South Florida property holdings during David’s growing involvement with Inter Miami.That Miami apartment was later sold for about $24.6 million in 2026, according to property reporting. The couple also bought a waterfront Miami Beach mansion in 2024 for about $72.3 million, below its $80 million asking price.So, while the Beverly Hills home is now part of the Beckhams’ past property portfolio, its sale marked an important point in the family’s move away from their old Los Angeles base and toward a stronger connection with Miami.
Article Summary: David and Victoria Beckham bought the Beverly Hills property in 2007 after David moved to Los Angeles to begin his Major League Soccer career. The Italian villa- style property had about 11,500 to more than 13,000 square feet of living space. It had six bedrooms, multiple living areas, a library, an elevator and a media and music room. The house was also surrounded by gates and landscaping that gave the family a high level of privacy.

Lauren Steadman has added another major title to a career already filled with Paralympic medals. The British athlete won Celebrity MasterChef 2026 after beating Olympic weightlifter Emily Campbell and Love Island star Shakira Khan in the BBC One final. Steadman impressed judges Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli with a three-course menu, with her sticky toffee pudding playing an important part in the decision. The victory gives the 33-year-old another television success after Strictly Come Dancing and Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins. But away from TV, Steadman’s biggest achievements have come in swimming and paratriathlon.Steadman won the Celebrity MasterChef 2026 final on September 18 after the three finalists were asked to cook a three-course meal for Dent and Locatelli. The series started with 15 celebrities before the competition was reduced to the final three.Her menu began with pan-fried scallops in chilli butter, served with coconut and spinach lentil dahl puree and fresh apple batons. For the main course, she prepared beef Wellington with truffle mash, caramelised shallots, butternut squash puree, tenderstem broccoli and red wine jus.The dessert was a classic sticky toffee pudding with dates, caramel sauce and clotted cream ice cream.It proved to be a key moment in the final. Locatelli praised the pudding, while Dent also spoke highly of Steadman’s food.Steadman was visibly emotional after hearing the result. She said: “This is up there with a Paralympic gold medal. There haven’t been many moments when I have been left speechless but this is one of them.”The final followed several demanding challenges during the series. Steadman had already cooked for guests at Crufts and taken part in the Chef’s Table at The Ritz.Steadman’s final menu helped her secure the trophy, while also noting her earlier Paralympic success.Before becoming a television regular, Steadman built her name in elite sport. Born in Peterborough, she started swimming at a young age and represented Great Britain at the Beijing 2008 Paralympic Games when she was 15.She returned to the pool at London 2012. Her results did not bring a Paralympic medal, but the experience helped shape what came next.Steadman later moved into paratriathlon after her uncle, who is also a triathlete, encouraged her to try the sport. Her first British triathlon came in 2011, when she finished second.Her first Paralympic triathlon medal came at Rio 2016, where she won silver in the sport’s Paralympic debut. Five years later, she went one step further at Tokyo 2020, winning gold in the women’s PTS5 event.At Paris 2024, Steadman returned to the podium with bronze in the same classification. That gave her a full set of Paralympic triathlon medals: silver, gold and bronze.According to ParalympicsGB, Steadman is a three-time World Champion and has won eight European titles. She was also appointed MBE in the 2022 New Year Honours for services to triathlon.Steadman’s television career began long before Celebrity MasterChef. In 2018, she joined Strictly Come Dancing with professional dancer AJ Pritchard. She reached the semi-finals and became the first female contestant with a disability to take part in the BBC show.Her next major television challenge came with Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins. Steadman reached the final stage of the competition and was later crowned a joint winner of the series.She also appeared on Richard Osman’s House of Games before taking on Celebrity MasterChef in 2026.The television appearances have given audiences a different look at Steadman outside competition. Strictly tested her dancing, SAS put her through demanding physical and mental challenges, while MasterChef moved her into a completely different setting.Her professional work also includes motivational speaking and business activity. Steadman’s official website describes her work around mindset, performance and helping people deal with perceived barriers. She is also linked to Sizu, a motivational wellness clothing brand.According to LatestCelebArticles, Lauren Steadman’s net worth is estimated at between $1 million and $5 million. However, the website does not provide financial records or details showing how the figure was calculated, so the estimate cannot be independently confirmed. Her income is linked to her sporting career, television appearances, sponsorships and other professional work.The University of Portsmouth’s profile of the Paralympic champion confirms that, alongside her sporting and television career, she has also been involved in entrepreneurial work.Her income has come from several areas over the years, including elite sport, television work, sponsorships, speaking engagements and business projects. Her exact earnings from Celebrity MasterChef and her other television appearances have not been publicly disclosed.Steadman also has a strong academic background. She studied Psychology at the University of Portsmouth, graduating with a first-class degree in 2014. She later completed an MSc in Business and Management with distinction in 2017.The University of Portsmouth has highlighted both degrees in its profiles of Steadman. The university also notes her sporting achievements, including her Rio silver, Tokyo gold and Paris bronze.Away from sport and television, Steadman has generally kept her personal life private. She has spoken publicly about the role her family played in her early sporting journey, while her uncle was the person who encouraged her to try triathlon after her swimming career.Claims about her current relationship should be treated carefully because reliable public sources do not provide enough information to independently confirm the reported details about a boyfriend named Danny.Steadman has built a career across several very different fields. She went from a teenage Paralympic swimmer to a world-class paratriathlete, won gold at Tokyo 2020, returned for bronze in Paris, appeared on major British television shows and has now added the Celebrity MasterChef trophy to her record.
Article Summary: Lauren Steadman won Celebrity MasterChef 2026 on September 18. She beat Olympic weightlifter Emily Campbell and Love Island star Shakira Khan in the BBC One final. Steadman impressed judges Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli with a three- course menu, with her sticky toffee pudding playing an important part in the decision.

Why the Gisele Bundchen and Tom Brady story still matters for modern marriages

Long before "work-life balance" became a boardroom buzzword, one of football's greatest champions was learning that lesson at his own kitchen table. Back in 2020, Tom Brady opened up about a letter from his wife, Gisele Bundchen , that changed how he showed up at home. Their story still resonates today, offering a timeless reminder about partnership, fairness, and what it really takes to keep a marriage strong.Speaking with radio host Howard Stern, Brady recalled a moment from 2018 that forced him to rethink his priorities. Gisele had written him a letter laying out her frustration. She felt like the football season would end, and instead of turning his attention home, Brady would dive straight into business deals and offseason training.“She didn’t feel like I was doing my part for our family,” he said. “She felt like I would play football all season and she would take care of the house and all of a sudden when the season would end, I would be like, ‘Great, let me get into all my other business activities. Let me get into my football training.’ And she’s sitting there going, ‘Well, when are you going to do things for the house? When are you going to take the kids to school and do that?’”Brady didn't sugarcoat how that realization hit him. He admitted, "I had to, like, check myself." His wife had made her point clearly. She had goals of her own too, and she wasn't willing to put them on hold indefinitely while he chased his.That single letter pushed Brady to skip a few team activities so he could be more present at home, whether that meant school runs or simply being around for his kids. It's a small shift on paper, but for a professional athlete at the peak of his career, it spoke volumes.This isn't just a celebrity anecdote. Women still shoulder a disproportionate share of unpaid household work compared to men, according to research from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.That imbalance, valued in the trillions of dollars annually, shows up in ordinary homes just as much as in the households of millionaires.Melinda Gates faced a similar dynamic in her own marriage. When her daughter started kindergarten, Melinda wanted to wait a year because of a long commute. Bill insisted on enrolling her right away, then asked what would make it easier. Her answer was simple: he could drive.Brady's takeaway echoed that same lesson about partnership. He put it plainly: relationships only work when both people benefit, not just one. Years later, his words still hold up as a reminder that even the busiest, most successful people have to make room for the people they love.

Article Title: What happened to Alonzo Menifield? 38-year-old boxing superstar overcomes all odds against Iwo Baraniewski despite scary thumb injury
Article Text:

How Alonzo Menifield beat Iwo Baraniewski at UFC 331 with a broken thumb

Alonzo Menifield's thumb injury and the reaction inside the arena

Alonzo Menifield was supposed to be the next name on Iwo Baraniewski's knockout list. The 38-year-old had other plans on Saturday night at UFC 331, and a hand injury that made an entire arena groan did not change them.The light heavyweight bout opened the main card at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. Baraniewski, an undefeated Polish fighter with a habit of finishing early, had never needed the judges before. Menifield, a veteran with a dozen UFC wins, changed that and collected the win.Alonzo Menifield and Iwo Baraniewski met on Saturday, September 19, and the first round belonged to the Polish fighter. Baraniewski, riding a run of first-round knockouts, stunned Menifield more than once with his right hook and put the 38-year-old on the mat. Menifield gave up his back but survived, then found his footing in a late scramble, according to LowKick MMA's round-by-round account.Round two followed a similar script. Menifield started fast and landed heavy shots. Baraniewski kept walking forward anyway and found the cleaner combinations.Before round three, the doctor took a look at Menifield's hand. MMA Junkie described a deep cut, and the fight went on. The veteran opened the final round by stunning Baraniewski, but both men were tired by then.They spent long stretches in the clinch until the referee split them up. After the restart, Baraniewski pushed the pace and landed the harder strikes until the bell.The scorecards told a tight story. Two judges gave it 29-28 to Menifield, and one went 28-29 the other way. It was Baraniewski's first career loss and his first trip to a decision, which left the Polish fighter at 9-1.The full extent of the damage only came out after the decision was read. During the post-fight interview with Joe Rogan , Menifield held the thumb up to the camera. The Big Lead reported that a bone was sticking through, and MMA Junkie said the crowd let out a loud groan.The reports do not agree on when it happened. The Big Lead placed the injury in the first round, while MMA Junkie pointed to the doctor's check ahead of round three. LowKick MMA called it a broken thumb and said Menifield fought through it in the third.Fans did not need long to react. Barstool Sports posted, "Alonzo Menifield’s thumb is backwards and he’s still letting it fly" (@barstoolsports). Championship Rounds wrote, "ALONZO MENIFIELD'S THUMB HAS A BONE STICKING OUT" (@ChampRDS).The Big Lead reported that Menifield will not be back in action anytime soon, and none of the three reports give a recovery timeline. The 38-year-old is now 19-6-1 with 11 knockouts and has won two straight.
Article Summary: Alonzo Menifield beat Iwo Baraniewski at UFC 331 despite a broken thumb. The 38-year-old is now 19-6-1 with 11 knockouts and has won two straight. The Polish fighter is now 9-1, his first career loss.

Article Title: Japan opens Asian Games 2026 with a heartfelt celebration of culture and unity in Aichi-Nagoya
Article Text:
Nagoya wows the continent

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Who will open India’s medal tally?

NAGOYA: Almost three hours before the start of the Asian Games opening ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, spectators had begun filling the expansive, multi-tiered stands. The 35,000-capacity venue was not full, but that did little to dampen the celebration that followed.The first glimpse was of a gigantic heart. But this was not merely about love. The heart-shaped stage, bathed in white, underlined the ceremony’s theme — Harmonic Hea-rtbeat. Like matcha, sake or sushi, themes and cultures can be an acquired taste. Whi-le some found the nearly two-hour spectacle underwhelming, from a Japanese perspective it was a celebration steeped in tradition, culture, diversity and technology.The evening began with a pre-ceremony performance by the Shigo Bonote Preservation Society and the hugely popular INI boy band. The ceremony itself opened with dancers in heart-shaped attire and a performance by celebrated Japanese violinist Taro Hakase. With Japanese royalty led by emperor Naruhito and empress Masako, International Olympic Committee president Kirsty Coventry and Olympic Council of Asia president Sheikh Joaan Hamad Al Thani among the dignitaries in attendance, the Japanese national flag was raised by members of the Japan Self-Defence Forces.Volunteers carrying heart-shaped placards bearing the names of participating countries then led the athletes and officials into the stadium. The Indians, looking dapper in deep blue, received a warm welcome, though the loudest cheers in the stadium were reserved for the hosts.The centrepiece of the night was a replica of Nagoya Castle, placed at the heart of the stage and illuminated in a kaleidoscope of colours.The heart-shaped cauldron was lit by five-time Asian Games champion and hammer throw legend Shigenobu Murofushi and his son Koji, the 2004 Olympic hammer throw champion.Sheikh Joaan in his speech said, “Tonight, the eyes of Asia and much of the world turn to Japan. What we will see over the next few days will inspire us. It will move us. And it will remind us of what we are capable of when we come together for Asia.”With One Asia, One Heart at the centre of the ceremony, the troubles of the past few days, which had put Nagoya’s ability to host the Games under scrutiny, seemed to fade into the background, at least for the night.The ceremony ended with fireworks lighting up the night sky, offering a fitting hope that the Games, too, will shine as brightly.India, who returned from the 2022 Hangzhou Games with a record 107 medals, will begin their quest to better that haul on Sunday, with three disciplines offering early opportunities to get on the board.All eyes will be on the Aichi Prefectural Shooting Ra-nge, with India expected to be in the thick of action, fighting for a podium finish. Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod will comp-ete in the women’s 10m air rif-le, with medals at stake in bo-th the team and individual ev-ents. In women’s cricket, defe-nding champions India face Bangladesh in the semifinal. A win will assure India of a m-edal. There could also be an interesting twist to India’s medal-opening narrative. In teqball, two bronze medals are up for grabs, while Suraj Singh will compete in the men’s changquan event, a medal event on the day, in wushu.

India, who returned from the 2022 Hangzhou Games with a record 107 medals, will begin their quest to better that haul on Sunday. All eyes will be on the Aichi Prefectural Shooting Ra-nge, with India expected to be in the thick of action.

Article Title: "She’s trying to be the general manager of the team": How Bill Belichick finally addressed Jordon Hudson’s UNC role and called one major assumption “so ridiculous”
Article Text:
Bill Belichick breaks his silence on Jordon Hudson’s UNC role (Getty Images)

What did Bill Belichick say about Jordon Hudson’s role at UNC?

Does Jordon Hudson have an official role with UNC football?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bill Belichick has finally offered a fuller explanation of Jordon Hudson’s role around his move to North Carolina, pushing back on the idea that she had influence over the Tar Heels’ football operation. In an interview with The Wall Street Journal, Belichick said Hudson helped coordinate parts of his schedule outside the university but had no official role with UNC football. He also took direct aim at a narrative that portrayed her as trying to control the program, calling that suggestion “so ridiculous.” The comments give Belichick’s clearest account yet of how a personal scheduling request became a much bigger story.Bill Belichick said the confusion began when he joined North Carolina and was still juggling several commitments away from coaching. At the time, he was working on television projects, a radio show and a book while taking charge of the Tar Heels.That workload led him to ask UNC staff to send requests related to his personal appearances to Hudson so she could help coordinate them separately from his university responsibilities.“When I took the job here, it was December, and at that time I was doing five TV shows, the radio show, I had a book coming out. I had a lot of other things going on when I took the job,” Belichick said.He said that request was later presented in a very different light.“So, I sent an email when I got here and I said, 'Can you please forward any requests to Jordon about my personal appearances so that I can work and coordinate them outside the university?' Didn't have anything to do with the university. Well, that was leaked and released as 'Jordon's involved in every single thing that I do and she's copied on every email.' That's just a flat-out lie.”Belichick was even more blunt when discussing the suggestion that Hudson wanted power within the football program.“The way the story was picked up was a long way from that. Like, 'She's trying to be the general manager of the team,' and it's so ridiculous.”According to Belichick, she does not. He made a distinction between helping with parts of his life away from North Carolina football and having a role inside the program.“There are some things that she helps me schedule or look at,” he said. “It's not North Carolina stuff.”That clarification matters because Hudson’s presence around Belichick had previously generated questions about how much access or influence she had around the Tar Heels. Belichick had also publicly said in 2025 that Hudson had no role with the UNC football program.Hudson has remained largely out of the public discussion surrounding UNC this season. The Tar Heels opened the 2026 campaign 2-0 under Belichick before their ACC matchup with Clemson, keeping the focus increasingly on football rather than the off-field questions that followed the coach during his first season.For Belichick, though, the issue was worth addressing again because he believes a simple request tied to his personal schedule was turned into something much larger. His latest comments draw a clear boundary: Hudson may assist him with personal matters, but he says that should not be confused with running, influencing or managing UNC football.
Article Summary: Belichick says Hudson helped coordinate parts of his schedule outside the university but had no official role with UNC football. He also took direct aim at a narrative that portrayed her as trying to control the program. The comments give Belichick’s clearest account yet of how a personal scheduling request became a much bigger story.

The heavyweight bout sat on the UFC 331 main card, and few people saw a finish that quick coming.It came down to one exchange. Sharaf pushed forward from the opening bell and forced Steveson to give ground. Steveson dodged a right hand, but the miss left him open. Sharaf answered with a left hook that landed flush at the 10-second mark and dropped him. A few ground shots followed, and the referee stopped it at 12 seconds.Steveson entered as a -2400 favorite, backed by his Olympic gold medal in wrestling and a 4-0 record.Sharaf, a former United States Marine, was a +1500 underdog. Diaz first used it after handing Conor McGregor his first UFC defeat. The Crypto.com Arena crowd went wild.Sharaf then turned to the people who doubted him. "I believed in myself when nobody believed in me," he said. Article Title: Separated from their own, these Kuno cheetahs found brothers in each other
Article Text:
An unlikely bond: Male cheetahs CCB4 (left) and KNG23 (right) have come to enjoy each other’s company





BHOPAL: One was born in India while the other flew thousands of kilometres by a special aircraft from Botswana. Though born to different mothers, they are brothers, not by blood but bonding. Deep in the wilds of Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno, two male cheetahs — coded as KNG23 and CCB4 — have developed an unusual social bond, offering a rare insight into how these felines can form lifelong relationships despite not growing up together.Their story, highlighted in the latest newsletter issued by Kuno authorities, has emerged as one of the most unusual behavioural developments in four remarkable years of Project Cheetah.KNG23 was born in India to cheetah Nirva, while CCB4 was among the felines translocated from the African wilds of Botswana. The two unrelated males were brought together after separate periods of isolation. What began as a cautious introduction has evolved into a close social association, with the two now following each other, hunting and feeding together, calling to each other and even grooming one another.The Kuno field team has also observed the two supporting each other when challenged by another coalition.Such behaviour has prompted the team to closely monitor whether their association develops into a stable coalition.Male cheetahs are typically social animals, known to form coalitions, most commonly between brothers from the same litter. Such groups can help males defend territories, hunt and protect kills, patrol their range and confront rivals and predators.KNG23 and CCB4, however, do not fit the familiar pattern. They are unrelated, coming from different countries and growing up in different habitats.However, the stories of how they got separated from their own do bear an uncanny similarity. KNG23 was separated from his mother, brother and sister around March 2026, after suffering a minor injury that required isolation, while CCB4 was separated from his two sisters around the same period.The two males were subsequently introduced to each other.Even after KNG23 recovered and was reunited with his family, he continued to show an interest in CCB4 while the two remained separated by a fence. KNG23 was released into the wild with his mother, brother and sister on May 30. After several weeks, he was injured again in late July and brought back for treatment. By then, CCB4 was alone, as his two sisters had moved into the wild. The two males were again placed close to each other to explore whether their association could develop further.Their first introduction was peaceful. When the fence was removed, both appeared relaxed and comfortable in each other’s presence. The crucial test came when a kill was provided. However, even the prey could put a strain on their relationship, as they both shared the meal without showing any aggression or confrontation.Over the following days, stronger signs of social bonding emerged. KNG23 began following CCB4 closely and sitting beside him. They continued hunting and feeding together. When one moved out of sight, the other responded with the characteristic chirping call used by cheetahs to maintain contact. They were also observed grooming each other, Kuno officials noted in the newsletter.The field team said the two are now displaying several behaviours associated with coalition formation, including remaining together, following one another, hunting and feeding together and mutual grooming.Officials, however, cautioned that sharing a kill or spending time together alone does not establish a coalition. If the association develops into a stable coalition, it could potentially be the first documented coalition between two unrelated male cheetahs originating from different countries, they added.
Article Summary: KNG23 was born in India to cheetah Nirva, while CCB4 was among the felines translocated from the African wilds of Botswana. The two unrelated males were brought together after separate periods of isolation. What began as a cautious introduction has evolved into a close social association.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu on AI doom fears: ‘Without scientific scepticism, we risk being delusional’
Article Text:
Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu

Sridhar Vembu says AI scepticism must stay grounded in science

James Maynard says he was wrong about AI predictions

Sridhar Vembu says conviction and scepticism both matter

Zoho founder and chief scientist Sridhar Vembu has shared his view on the growing debate over whether AI could pose serious risks to humanity. Sridhar Vembu said he has not bought into AI doom scenarios, but believes people should remain open to changing their views as AI models become more capable. Vembu was responding to a post by American physicist Steve Hsu, who shared comments from Fields Medalist James Maynard on X. Maynard said he had been sceptical of earlier AI predictions that sounded like science fiction but now takes the risks more seriously because many of those predictions have proved more accurate than he expected.Sridhar Vembu said people need both personal conviction and scientific scepticism when thinking about AI and its future.“I have not bought into the AI doom scenarios,” Vembu wrote on X, pointing to Maynard's changing position as an example of what he described as a scientific attitude.“Fields Medalist James Maynard teaches us the scientific attitude about this: he has been highly sceptical of claims of AI doom but as the models demonstrate higher and higher capability levels, he is taking them more seriously now.”Steve Hsu's post quoted Maynard discussing how his view of AI risks has changed.Maynard said he had followed AI for some time but had been sceptical of predictions that appeared to come from science fiction.“I've been interested and I've been following AI, but I've heard all these predictions that just sound like sci-fi and I've been consistently dismissive and skeptical of all of them.”He then acknowledged that his earlier view had been wrong.“But I've been consistently wrong. The people who sound like they're talking from a sci-fi novel are the people who've been making much much more accurate predictions.”Maynard concluded that AI risks should not simply be dismissed as hype.Vembu said personal conviction helps people continue working toward a goal, while scientific scepticism can prevent people from becoming disconnected from evidence.“Our own hunches and convictions allow us to pursue and stick to a course of action and scientific scepticism keeps us grounded in reality,” he wrote.He added:“Without a strong internal conviction, our actions lack the will power to succeed. Without scientific scepticism, we risk being delusional.”
Article Summary: Sridhar Vembu says people need both personal conviction and scientific scepticism when thinking about AI and its future. He was responding to a post by American physicist Steve Hsu, who shared comments from Fields Medalist James Maynard. Maynard said he had been sceptical of earlier AI predictions that sounded like science fiction but now takes the risks more seriously.

Article Title: Offshore wind farms may be quietly stealing rain from Europe's coasts; study says: The more energy turbines pull from the wind, the less...
Article Text:
Representative image

Turbines slow the wind and stir up the air above the sea

Ten years of weather data went into the North Sea rainfall model

The study tested an extreme wind buildout, not Europe's actual plan

Europe is counting on offshore wind to move away from fossil fuels, and the North Sea is at the centre of that plan. The European Union wants 300 gigawatts of offshore wind capacity by 2050. A new study from Germany suggests turbines at that scale could do more than generate electricity. They could also change where rain falls.Researchers at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon found that very large offshore wind farm clusters may push more rain over the sea and leave parts of the coastline drier. In their simulations, coastal areas in Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom saw rainfall drop by up to 15%. The findings were published in the journal Communications Earth & Environment.A wind turbine works by taking energy out of moving air. The wind behind it ends up slower and more turbulent.That turbulence mixes different layers of the atmosphere. Moist air gets pushed upward, where it cools, condenses and forms clouds. The result is more rain directly over the wind farms.The catch is that air can only carry so much moisture. When more of it falls over the sea, less is left by the time the air reaches land.Coastal regions downwind get less rain as a result.The team at Hereon's Institute of Coastal Systems - Analysis and Modeling used a high-resolution regional climate model called COSMO-CLM. The simulations ran on weather data from 2008 to 2017. Using a full decade smoothed out the effect of any single unusual year and gave a clearer view of long-term patterns.The model included existing wind farms and every zone marked for future development across the North Sea and the Baltic Sea."Our work helps ensure that the further expansion of offshore wind energy in Europe can be aligned with the requirements of climate protection, environmental protection and coastal management," said Dr Naveed Akhtar, the study's lead author.The scenario was extreme by design. The researchers assumed maximum turbine deployment across all designated areas, which pushed installed capacity well past the 300 GW target. The goal was to make any climate effect large enough to detect and measure. It is not a forecast of what Europe will build.The results also describe long-term weather averages. They do not mean a specific town will miss rain on a specific day. Earlier Hereon research has shown that farm size, layout and turbine spacing affect how strongly turbines change the atmosphere, so a smaller or more spread-out buildout may have a milder effect.So will Europe's coasts lose rain? That depends on how the continent builds. The researchers are not arguing against offshore wind. They want more realistic scenarios tested for turbine density, farm size and placement, and they plan to study effects on the ocean and marine life next. For countries that share the same weather systems, where a wind farm goes may matter as much as how much power it produces.
Article Summary: Turbines slow the wind and stir up the air above the sea. Moist air gets pushed upward, where it cools, condenses and forms clouds. The result is more rain directly over the wind farms. When more of it falls over the sea, less is left by the time the air reaches land.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.
